clue.text: Revered husband made a confession

parts.note: to allow something is to admit or confess it

explanation.surface: A respected husband owned up to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hallowed is held sacred and deeply honoured, a synonym for revered.

clue.text: Time invested in an unusual form of etching

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: time is placed inside the other word

parts.note: quaint means oddly old-fashioned or unusual

explanation.surface: Time was spent on a curious kind of engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatint is an etching technique producing tonal areas like watercolour washes.

clue.text: There's fabric in nets fashioned for this sport

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen or cotton fabric

indicators.note: the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: Cloth is woven into nets made for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges IN NETS to give TENNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the full name of the racket sport, an example of a sport.

clue.text: Protective garment for poet involved with war

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together

explanation.surface: A protective coat suited to a poet caught up in conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles FOR POET and WAR together; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof is a coat that keeps rain out, a garment that protects.

clue.text: Critically examine direction given in short reference book

indicators.note: the direction is put inside the shortened book

parts.note: dict is the short form of dictionary
SSE, south-south-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Scrutinise the guidance in a pocket dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect an argument is to analyse it in detail, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Father of modern artistic movement

definitions.meaning: a childish word for one's father

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a baby name for a father and the name of the Dada art movement.

clue.text: Tropical author

parts.note: a writer known for novels named after the tropics, Cancer and Capricorn

explanation.definitionFit: Henry Miller wrote Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn, hence a tropical author.

clue.text: Horse, in one type of combat, not wounded

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the combat word

parts.note: unarmed combat is fighting without weapons
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A horse in hand-to-hand fighting comes through unhurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Unharmed means uninjured, a direct synonym for not wounded.

clue.text: Doing nothing during first part of play — performing later

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the winter'
the first part of a play is Act I
an actor who is on is performing on stage

explanation.surface: Someone idles through the opening of a play, only going on stage later.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is the state of being idle, a noun matching the gerund phrase.

clue.text: Intellectually get the better of old university idiot

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A clever student gets one over on a foolish former college mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit is to defeat someone by being cleverer, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Lamb's full of a singular flavour in this part of the country

indicators.note: the pen name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tang is a sharp flavour

explanation.surface: Lamb served with a particular taste is a regional speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' looks like meat, but it is the essayist Charles Lamb, whose pen name was Elia. EAST ANGLIA is the eastern region of England around Norfolk and Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: East Anglia is a region of eastern England, an example of a part of the country.

clue.text: Mask fell

definitions.meaning: to mask something is to conceal it from view
a fell is an animal's skin or pelt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to conceal and an animal's skin, matching the two senses.

clue.text: Peaceful border in Asian region

parts.note: pacific means peaceable or calm
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A calm frontier in part of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific Rim is the area of countries bordering the Pacific, including east Asia.

clue.text: Having had the wind up, female put straight

parts.note: to righten is to set right

explanation.surface: A woman was scared after setting things straight.
explanation.walkthrough: To have the wind up is British slang for being scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the wind up means being scared, so this matches the past participle meaning scared.

clue.text: Some brain shown by Caesar, initially, before his war

indicators.note: take just the first letter of Caesar

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
bellum is Latin for war, Caesar's own language

explanation.surface: Caesar displays intellect before writing about his campaigns.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is the part of the brain at the back that controls movement, so it is some of the brain.

clue.text: Over time, heartless senator becomes powerful speaker

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes over, that is covers, the letter for time
the middle letter of the word is removed, its heart

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: Eventually a senator with no compassion turns into a forceful orator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central A of SENATOR to leave SENTOR, and 'Over' puts it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a Greek herald in Homer with a mighty voice, so his name means someone very loud.

clue.text: Light cooked meal for young children

parts.note: small means slight or light
a fry is a meal of fried food

explanation.surface: An easy fry-up for the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fry is an idiom for children or unimportant people.

clue.text: Saw what someone was saying

parts.note: seeing speech rather than hearing it, by watching the mouth move

explanation.definitionFit: To lip-read is to understand speech by watching lip movements, literally seeing what is said.

clue.text: Girl turned up with emperor in Indian city

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Irma is a girl's name
a tsar was the emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: A girl showed up with a ruler in a city in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in Punjab, India, home of the Golden Temple.

clue.text: Here and now

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both being in attendance and the current moment.

clue.text: In hands of orthopaedists, etc.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A list of things found in the hands of bone specialists trails off.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is commonly rendered as the phrase meaning and the rest of that kind.

clue.text: Daughter put on a protective covering of reversible fabric

parts.note: a mask covers and protects the face

explanation.surface: A girl puts on a face covering made of two-sided cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a woven fabric whose pattern shows on both sides, so it can be reversed.

clue.text: Save king in old vessel

parts.note: save and bar both mean except
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Rescue a monarch aboard an ancient ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A bark or barque is a sailing ship, a word now used mostly in older or poetic writing.

clue.text: Judiciously selected term of French

parts.note: a French expression meaning the precisely right word, chosen with care

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means exactly the right word for the occasion, a carefully chosen term.

clue.text: Old invader of England prepared for sacking

definitions.meaning: one of a Germanic tribe that settled in Kent in the fifth century
a plant fibre processed for making sacks

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Germanic invader of Britain and a fibre used for sacking.

clue.text: Votes against euros finally, holding pound as important

indicators.note: the votes word contains the letter for pound

parts.note: the noes are the votes against in a division
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: take only the last letter of the word euros

explanation.surface: Opponents of the euro ultimately consider sterling just as important.
explanation.definitionFit: No less means equally, so something no less important is as important.

clue.text: This madman messed up tsarina endlessly

indicators.note: messed signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A deranged figure muddled the Russian empress to no end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TSARINA to TSARIN; 'messed' scrambles UP with TSARIN. Rasputin was the mystic who held sway over the last tsarina, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin, the Mad Monk of the Romanov court, is a famous example of a madman.

clue.text: Returned revision to book's author that shows extent of clean-up

indicators.note: the word for revision is read backwards

parts.note: an edit is a revision of a text
Mark is the author of the Gospel of Mark, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: An edited manuscript goes back to its writer.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIDEMARK is the dirty line left round a bath or on skin showing how far washing reached.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line marking how far water or washing reached, showing the extent of cleaning.
